elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "The access and rights to use granted to the Company under this Section 1.4 shall extend to the Company's affiliates upon written notice to HDI." The defined "Company" is The Deerskin Companies, Inc. alone, so this adds genuine (non-duplicative) affiliate coverage.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Neither Section 1.4 as rendered nor the inserted sentence mentions contractors, agents or service providers acting on the Company's behalf; the grant runs only to the Company and its affiliates.
Section 1.4 grants access/use rights for the hosting arrangement with no perpetuity language, and no perpetual-on-payment concept was added; the grant's duration is left tied to the Agreement term.

No "irrevocable" wording appears in Section 1.4 or the insertion. (Favourably, nothing in the rendered text makes the grant revocable or suspendable at HDI's discretion, so walk-away territory is avoided, but the affirmative irrevocability element is absent.)

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: The rendered excerpt contains only Sections 1.4 and 10.3; the Agreement's termination provisions are not before me, so I cannot confirm whether termination of the access/use rights is limited to uncured material breach.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Section 10.3: "This Agreement shall be binding upon, and shall inure to the benefit of and be enforceable by, the parties hereto and their respective legal representatives, successors and assigns" — no consent condition or anti-assignment restriction is imposed, so the Section 1.4 rights pass to and are enforceable by the Company's successors.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: The added sentence extends the Section 1.4 access and use rights to "the Company's affiliates upon written notice to HDI" — exactly the notice-conditioned affiliate coverage the fallback requires.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: Existing Section 10.3 makes the Agreement (including the Section 1.4 rights) enforceable by the parties' "successors and assigns" with no consent gate; the residual "no other person shall acquire or have any rights" sentence excludes third parties, not successors.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: affiliate coverage on written notice is created by the inserted sentence in Section 1.4, and successor/M&A transferability already exists in Section 10.3's successors-and-assigns language, which contains no consent or anti-assignment restriction.

Preferred level is not complete. To reach it the drafter would need to (i) add "and contractors acting on the Company's behalf" to the Section 1.4 grant, (ii) state that rights paid for in full are perpetual and irrevocable, and (iii) confirm/insert that the subscription access right may be terminated only for uncured material breach — none of which appear in the operative text.

Minimality holds: a single additive sentence, no deletions or paraphrase of surrounding language, no survival tails, expense or procedure extras, and no duplication — "Company" is defined as The Deerskin Companies, Inc. alone, so affiliates were genuinely outside the grant.

Intent is preserved: the insertion is scoped expressly to "this Section 1.4", leaves HDI's service obligations, bandwidth commitments and Section 10.3 untouched, introduces no undefined term beyond the ordinary "affiliates", and creates no dangling cross-reference or contradictory retained sentence. Note that "affiliates" is used undefined; if the Agreement has no Affiliate definition, consider adding a short parenthetical definition rather than leaving it to construction.
No new Vendor-side assignment exception or other counterparty benefit was granted, so the intent test on successor/licence-transfer edits is satisfied.
